key_insight: A curriculum masking strategy for single-encoder masked-sequence transformers encourages stronger cross-attention from harmony to melody, enabling the model to better exploit melodic cues and generalize to out-of-domain melodies.
problem_solved: Existing training curricula (inspired by discrete diffusion) produce weak cross-attention between melody and harmony, causing generated accompaniments to underuse melodic information and fail to generalize beyond training distributions.
method: Design a progressive masking curriculum that controls which tokens (melody vs. harmony) are masked and how masking difficulty increases during training to prioritize melody–harmony interactions.
Train a single-encoder transformer as a masked sequence model using the curriculum so the model learns to attend to melody tokens when reconstructing harmony.
Evaluate attention patterns and generalization to out-of-domain melodies to verify improved melody-conditioned harmonization and robustness.
impact: A lightweight, training-time modification that significantly improves how conditional sequence models leverage context—useful for music generation and other conditional generation tasks where strong cross-conditioning is critical.
visual_elements: Curriculum timeline diagram showing mask ratio/type progression from easy → hard with examples of masked tokens
Side-by-side attention heatmaps (before vs. after curriculum) highlighting increased melody→harmony cross-attention
Architecture sketch of the single-encoder input sequence (melody + harmony tokens) with mask overlays
Example piano-rolls or MIDI snippets comparing harmonizations generated by baseline vs. curriculum-masked model
paper_title: Pay (Cross) Attention to the Melody: Curriculum Masking for Single-Encoder Melodic Harmonization
paper_authors: Maximos Kaliakatsos-Papakostas, Dimos Makris, Konstantinos Soiledis, Konstantinos-Theodoros Tsamis, Vassilis Katsouros
